 ORDER
With the consent of learned counsel for the appellant, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal, by the claimant has been filed by the appellant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of award dated 26.02.2022 passed by Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panna in MACC No.56/2019 seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to Ex.D/1 and D/2 and deposition of non applicant witness Rahul Singh submits that photocopy of Insurance policy filed in the case with respect to tractor bearing Registration No.MP-35-AA-3951 is fake one.
Correct policy is Ex.D/1 and insurance policy of trolley is Ex.D/2.
It is also urged that at the time of accident, respondent Dharam Das was travelling in the tractor.
In view of above, Insurance company is not liabile to pay the compensation as sitting capacity of tractor/trolley is nil.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal be allowed and insurance company be exonerated from liability to pay compensation.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record of the case.
5. So far as liability of insurance company is concerned, in FIR Ex.P/2, it is mentioned that at the time of accident deceased, Kissu @ Krisanavtar Yadav and Dharam Yadav were sitting on the tractor.
6. Perusal of deposition of injured Dharam Das reveals that he has not specifically mentioned in his deposition as to whether, at the time of accident, he was sitting on tractor or trolley.
But as seating capacity of passenger is nil in both tractor and trolley.
Hence, in view of principle of law laid down in the case of Bhav Singh Vs. Savirani 2007 SCC Online 412, Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Bhav Singh Vs. Savirani 2007 SCC Online 412
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In view of law laid in Bhav Singh (supra) and in view of FIR Ex.P/2 and deposition of injured Dharam Das, in this Court's considered opinion, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and insurance company(Original Claim Petition respondents No.3 and 5) is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation.
